newsitem.title: USA: Dow snares record close after early 53-point drop.
newsitem.headline: Dow snares record close after early 53-point drop.

text.p: The Dow industrials roared back from a 53-point deficit to snare a new record, boosted by a large afternoon buy program and a turnaround in bonds, but volume was sleepy ahead of the Fed's policy meeting Tuesday.

"We're just seeing statistical noise in anticipation of the Fed meeting tomorrow. There were some nervous Nellies selling stock at the open and then this afternoon we had bargain-hunters," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon and Farrell. The Dow rose six to about 5895, topping last Monday's 5889.20.

The broader market remained weak, with the S&P 500 off fractionally to about 686. The Nasdaq Composite lost eight to about 1211. Losers outpaced gainers 7-4 on NYSE volume of about 295 million shares, the slowest so far this month. Volume was also thinned by the Yom Kippur holiday.

The long bond erased earlier modest losses and rose 10/32 to yield 7.02 percent after an unidentified Federal Reserve source reassured Wall Street that the Fed remains vigilant in its inflation fight. The source told Reuters the Fed views a zero to two percent range on core Consumer Price Index as price stability.

Largely due to the aggressive 1994 preemptive tightening cycle, the Fed has brought core CPI down from around 4.9 percent in 1991 -- when the expansion kicked off in the second quarter -- to 2.6 percent in the sixth year of the current cycle. Targetting core CPI as a guidline for monetary policy has been "informally adopted within the Fed," the Fed source said.

Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst, said the Dow returned to record territory "as bonds came back...the Reuter story that the Fed is targetting core CPI as a guide for monetary policy and a big buy program."
Biriniyi Associates said it tracked one large afternoon buy program that added 30 Dow points and then a smaller one that added 3.7 points.
"But today is one of those days you write off as the blank space before the news. Everyone is watching for tomorrow," Crane said.
A slim majority on Wall Steet expect a modest 25 basis point tightening, according to a recent Reuter survey.
"If there's no change, the initial reaction for stocks will be positive, but I wouldn't be surprised to see bonds reverse course," Crane said.
"A modest tightening would have stocks give up a bit in the short-run and bonds would probably move a little lower initially and then rally," he added.
Few on Wall Street see a 50 basis point tightening, but expect stocks to be roiled on such an aggressive Fed move.

Among special situations, Missimo, the apparel designer that went public in February, tumbled 6-7/8 to 34-1/8. It warned that third-quarter earnings would fall far short of Street expectations after unusually high production costs that hurt gross margins for men's and women's autumn sportswear collections. Merrill Lynch downgraded the stock.

Templeton Russia Fund lost 1-1/4 to 21-1/2. Russian President Boris Yeltsin's doctors have recommended delaying heart surgery for Yeltsin for two months to let him build up more strength before the operation.

Lehman Brothers rose 1/8 to 22-7/8 after hitting an intraday high of 24-1/4. Lehman, whose shares rose Friday amid takeover speculation, said it knew of no business reason to account for the unusual acitivity in its shares and declined to confirm or deny if it was a possible takeover candidate.
Alcoa lost 1-7/8 to 58-5/8 and Alumax fell 5/8 to 32-1/2. Goldman cut the stocks to market perform from outperform.
Exide Electronics rose 3-1/2 to 12-5/8 after news it won an Air Force contract with a potential value of $625 million to provide and service power supply systems.

Diamond Shamrock rose 3/8 to 30-5/8 and Ultramar Corp added 1-3/8 to 29-7/8 after the companies agreed to a merger of equals in which each share of Diamond Shamrock will be converted into 1.02 shares of Ultramar.
Spine Tech rose 1-5/8 to 25-3/8 after the FDA approved its BAK Interbody Fusion System used to treat chronic low back pain caused by degenerative disc disease.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 8.22 to 1211.47.
The S&P 500 index fell 0.55 to 686.48.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
